anya: Heads-up — saw a weird resolution in prod for a header-driven route. client sent `x-model-alias: search-v2` but the request landed on `redwood-small-quant` instead of the pinned `redwood-search-2025-02`. :thinking:

sam: Hmm. Do we have rule ordering oddities? which route matched? any logs?

anya: Pasted the snippet from the routing-decider logs: `route=search, alias=search-v2 -> candidate aliases [search-v2, search-default] -> resolved candidate="search-default" -> pinned_v=redwood-small-quant (compat=false) -> fallback picked`. But compat=false is surprising — the model should be compatible for embeddings+chat.

matt: Can you paste the actual rule config? might be a header matcher + expression that triggers the default path.

anya: config excerpt: ```yaml
- match:
    path: /v1/search
    header: { x-model-alias: search-v2 }
  resolution:
    alias: search-v2
    prefer_pinned: true
    allow_compat_fallback: true
```

lina: Two things I want to call out: 1) `prefer_pinned` is currently only advisory in the decider, tie-breakers still use "priority" buckets. 2) `allow_compat_fallback` will let the legacy quantized variant be chosen if the compatibility check fails for the ideal one.

sam: So the decider saw compat=false for `redwood-search-2025-02`? what's causing that check to fail — dtype mismatch? kv-cache layout?

anya: Stack trace shows failure in the compatibility layer: `ModelSignatureMismatch: kv_cache_layout_v2 != kv_cache_layout_v1`. That error path currently increments fallback_count and emits telemetry but doesn't surface an explainable reason in the console.

matt: Ugh. It's the classic kv cache layout change between search model families. We should avoid silently falling back to a smaller quantized model: that can change output quality.

lina: Agreed. UX + policy change: when `prefer_pinned` is true, we should surface a policy violation and reject the request rather than falling back automatically, unless the route explicitly allows degraded fallbacks. Default behavior should be fail-fast.

sam: API semantics debate: Some customers expect graceful degradation (lower cost) when their pinned model is unavailable. Others expect strict pinning. We need a knob per-route: `pin_behavior: [strict|degrade|warn-only]`.

anya: +1 for explicit enum. Right now we have boolean `prefer_pinned` and `allow_compat_fallback` which combine into unclear behavior. `pin_behavior` is much clearer.

matt: Implementation notes: decider must evaluate candidate pool -> apply compatibility filter -> if none pass -> act according to `pin_behavior`. For `strict` return 425 with body explaining resolution (so client can retry with header override). For `degrade` pick next best and tag telemetry. For `warn-only` pick next best and emit warning.

lina: Also: console changes — surface resolved model and resolution reason in the per-route timeline (like: "resolved=redwood-small-quant reason=kv_cache_layout_mismatch pinned=redwood-search-2025-02 pin_behavior=degrade"). That will save hours debugging.

sam: Telemetry: add metrics `route.resolution_time_ms`, `route.fallback_count`, `route.pin_violation.{strict|degrade|warn}`, and log a `route_resolution_explain` event with fields: route, alias, pinned, chosen, reason.

anya: I can drive a small PR: add `pin_behavior` enum to routing DSL, update decider logic, add `route_resolution_explain` event. But before changing production semantics, we should run a canary with `warn-only` default and surface UX bits.

matt: Agree. Also add an alert rule: if `fallback_count` / `requests` > 0.5% for a route over 5m, page oncall. We don't want silent degradations.

deploy-bot: deploy started — routing-decider:v2 -> canary (10% traffic)

ops-bot: NOTE: canary targets are labeled `canary-198888`. Observability dashboards auto-created for `canary-198888` with resolution_explain logs enabled.

lina: Quick question for API: should we return a structured header when we reject because of strict pin? e.g., `x-resolve-error: pin-strict; pinned=redwood-search-2025-02; reason=kv_cache_layout_mismatch` so clients can surface?

sam: Yes. Structured header + 4xx with JSON body. Make the header machine-friendly (semicolon separated key=value pairs).

anya: I'll prototype patch + console patch to show resolution reason in the route activity panel. Plan: 1) DSL change, 2) decider change + unit tests for 3 behaviors, 3) canary with `warn-only`, 4) roll `strict` to customers who opt-in.

matt: Test matrix: pinned model available (ok), pinned incompatible (strict->reject, degrade->fallback+metric, warn-only->fallback+warn), pinned missing (same as incompatible), rate limit interactions (ensure fallback doesn't bypass per-model quotas).

lina: Also update docs/SDK: explain `pin_behavior` and a sample error response. Suggestion for console: add a toggle in the route editor labelled "Strict pinning (reject on incompatibility)" with tooltip.

sam: Nice work. once PR is ready ping me and I'll review. Also add an integration test that simulates kv-cache mismatch via a fake model metadata endpoint.

anya: Will do. filing a short RFC and the PR today. thanks all :thumbsup:
